overall_reason: A plain workspace sidebar whose three icons come from three different sets, so the small card has no single drawing style.

score.reason: T-SIGNATURE passes on the label-and-count list, but T-OWN-SYSTEM fails: Inbox is a filled tray, Project files a thin outline folder, Archive a heavy outline box at a larger size.

findings.evidence: The Inbox icon is a solid dark fill, the Project files folder a light thin outline, and the Archive box a thick outline that is visibly larger (tile 1440-00.png, x 415-433). The sweep's mixed_icons hit records the same mix.
findings.before: Three icon styles in a three-item list
findings.after: One icon set at one weight and size
findings.why: A list of three cannot hide a mixed set; it reads as icons pasted from different kits.

strengths: The list does its job: label, right-aligned count, nothing else.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent: no brand authority, audience or overrides were available, so the item was read as an Operate composition (CON-018).
T-RIVAL-NAME cap: the composition names no client, so every placeholder label holds under any rival; the cap at 5 was not applied and the test was used only to spot default copy.
T-IDEA-CARRIES: single composition, there is no second screen to carry the idea.
T-DELETE-PICTURE and T-PROMISE-PICTURED: no lead image and no marketing promise, except where a finding says so.
T-COVER-TEXT: no brand theme or motif to recognise.
The caption above some frames ('Considered composition' / 'Composition problem') is fixture text from the capture host and was not judged.
